symptoms_text: leaf spots shaped like eyes or spindles with grey centre and brown edge, spots join together and leaves dry up
label: rice_blast
treatment: Spray tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre at the first sign of spots; repeat after 12-15 days if new spots keep appearing. Do not apply extra urea while the disease is active.
prevention: Use blast resistant varieties recommended for your area|Treat seed with tricyclazole or carbendazim 2 g per kg before sowing|Give nitrogen in 3 split doses instead of one heavy dose|Keep the field and bunds free of grassy weeds
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in); Plantwise Knowledge Bank rice blast guide

symptoms_text: neck of the earhead turns black and breaks, grains remain empty, grey centred spots also on leaves
label: rice_blast

symptoms_text: leaf tips turn yellow white and dry from the edges downwards in stripes with a wavy border, leaves dry in patches after rains
label: rice_bacterial_leaf_blight
treatment: No spray cures it fully. Drain the field, stop urea top dressing for 2 weeks, and spray copper oxychloride 3 g per litre to limit spread. Remove badly infected clumps.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties|Do not clip seedling leaf tips at transplanting|Use balanced fertilizer and avoid heavy urea doses|Do not let irrigation water flow from an infected field into a healthy one
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in); IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank (knowledgebank.irri.org)

symptoms_text: young transplanted seedlings wilt and die suddenly, cut stem dipped in clear water shows milky ooze
label: rice_bacterial_leaf_blight

symptoms_text: round patches of plants suddenly dry up and look burnt, many small brown insects sitting on the stem base just above the water
label: rice_brown_planthopper
treatment: Drain the field for 3-4 days, then spray pymetrozine 50 WG 0.6 g per litre or dinotefuran 20 SG 0.4 g per litre aiming the nozzle at the base of the plants. Do not use synthetic pyrethroids - they make hoppers multiply faster.
prevention: Leave a 30 cm alleyway after every 8-10 rows so air and sunlight reach the base|Give nitrogen in 3 split doses|Avoid needless early sprays so spiders and mirid bugs that eat hoppers survive|Use BPH tolerant varieties where available
source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank BPH guide (knowledgebank.irri.org); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: plants yellowing and drying in circular patches called hopper burn, clouds of small insects jump up when the plants are disturbed
label: rice_brown_planthopper

symptoms_text: central shoot of young plant dries into a dead heart that pulls out easily, small bore holes in the stem
label: rice_stem_borer
treatment: Apply cartap hydrochloride 4G granules 8 kg per acre or chlorantraniliprole 0.4 GR 4 kg per acre in a thin film of standing water at tillering. Pull out and destroy dead hearts.
prevention: Set pheromone traps 3-4 per acre to catch moths|Release Trichogramma egg parasitoid cards where available|Cut stubble at ground level after harvest and plough it in|Avoid staggered late planting in one area
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: at earhead stage whole panicles turn white and stand empty, whiteheads come out easily when pulled
label: rice_stem_borer

symptoms_text: oval green grey water soaked patches on the leaf sheath near the water line, patches join into a snake skin pattern and climb up
label: rice_sheath_blight
treatment: Spray hexaconazole 5 EC 2 ml per litre or validamycin 3L 2.5 ml per litre directed at the lower part of the plants; repeat after 12-15 days if new patches appear.
prevention: Do not transplant too dense|Avoid excess nitrogen|Drain the field periodically instead of keeping deep water throughout|Remove grassy weeds on bunds that carry the fungus
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: boat shaped grey patches with brown border on the sheath at water level, upper leaves also getting patches in dense crop
label: rice_sheath_blight

symptoms_text: some grains in the earhead are replaced by round velvety green or orange powder balls
label: rice_false_smut
treatment: Spray copper oxychloride 2.5 g per litre or propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre at boot leaf stage before the ear comes out. Collect smut balls gently into a bag and destroy - do not shake them over the field.
prevention: Avoid very high urea doses|Sow and transplant on time|Use clean certified seed|Avoid ear-emergence coinciding with continuous drizzle where possible
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: greenish yellow dust balls on rice grains after flowering in cloudy weather
label: rice_false_smut

symptoms_text: leaves folded lengthwise and stitched with silk, white transparent streaks where the green layer has been eaten, folded leaves dry up
label: rice_leaf_folder
treatment: If more than 2 damaged leaves per plant, spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC 0.3 ml per litre or cartap hydrochloride 50 SP 2 g per litre.
prevention: Do not overuse urea|Keep bunds trimmed|Avoid unnecessary sprays so spiders and wasps survive|Use light traps to catch the moths
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: small green caterpillar found inside folded paddy leaf, white patches on leaves that later dry
label: rice_leaf_folder

symptoms_text: oval brown spots like sesame seeds with grey centre scattered on leaves, leaves turn yellow and dry, poor weak looking crop
label: rice_brown_spot
treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre or propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre at first appearance. Brown spot attacks weak crops - also correct the nutrition with the recommended potash and zinc dose.
prevention: Treat seed with carbendazim 2 g per kg - the fungus is seed borne|Apply balanced fertilizer as per soil test, the disease is worst in poor deficient soils|Avoid water stress|Use resistant varieties in disease prone areas
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: yellow leaves and many round brown spots on rice leaves, spots have dark border and lighter centre, grains also getting brown marks
label: rice_brown_spot

symptoms_text: small blue black spiny beetles sitting on leaves, white parallel streaks and window like scraped patches, leaf tips drying
label: rice_hispa
treatment: Clip and destroy leaf tips carrying eggs and grubs. If beetles are widespread, spray quinalphos 25 EC 2 ml per litre.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen|In hispa prone areas clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting|Keep field edges free of grasses
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: holes in leaves and small insects visible on the paddy leaves, leaves look scraped and whitish
label: rice_hispa

symptoms_text: yellow orange powder in long stripes along the veins of the leaf, powder sticks to the finger when rubbed, spreading in cold cloudy weather
label: wheat_yellow_rust
treatment: Spray propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre (about 200 ml per acre in 200 litres of water) as soon as the first pustules are seen, covering the whole field, not just patches; repeat after 15 days if it keeps spreading.
prevention: Grow the current rust resistant varieties recommended for your zone|Sow on time|Avoid excess nitrogen|Scout the crop weekly in cool humid weeks of January and February
source: ICAR yellow rust advisory (icar.org.in); ICAR-IIWBR Wheat Crop Health Newsletter (iiwbr.org.in)

symptoms_text: wheat leaves show lines of yellow dust and the field looks yellowish from a distance in january february
label: wheat_yellow_rust

symptoms_text: round orange brown powdery dots scattered all over the leaf, not in lines, appearing in the warmer weeks of late season
label: wheat_brown_rust
treatment: Spray propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre or tebuconazole 25.9 EC 1 ml per litre at first appearance; one more spray after 15 days if pustules increase.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties|Sow on time so grain filling escapes hot humid spells|Destroy volunteer wheat plants around the field
source: ICAR-IIWBR Wheat Crop Health Newsletter (iiwbr.org.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: scattered round rusty brown dots on wheat leaves that rub off as orange powder
label: wheat_brown_rust

symptoms_text: earheads come out as loose black powder instead of grain, the black dust blows away leaving a bare stalk
label: wheat_loose_smut
treatment: An infected plant cannot be saved. Cover smutted ears with a bag, pull them out and burn them so the powder does not spread. The fungus travels inside seed - next season treat seed with carboxin + thiram 75 WS 2 g per kg or tebuconazole 2 DS 1 g per kg.
prevention: Always sow certified treated seed|Never save seed from a field that had loose smut|Solar heat treatment (soak seed 4 hours in water then dry in hot sun) also disinfects small seed lots
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi crops (pau.edu); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: black powdery heads in wheat at earing, only the central stalk remains after wind
label: wheat_loose_smut

symptoms_text: white grey powdery patches on leaves and stem which later turn dirty grey, more in dense crop and cool cloudy weather
label: wheat_powdery_mildew
treatment: Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP 2.5 g per litre or propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre when the first patches appear.
prevention: Avoid very dense sowing|Avoid excess nitrogen|Grow resistant varieties in mildew prone hill and foothill areas
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Wheat (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: flour like white coating on wheat leaves that can be rubbed off
label: wheat_powdery_mildew

symptoms_text: groups of small soft green insects on earheads and upper leaves, sticky honeydew and black sooty layer on leaves
label: wheat_aphid
treatment: First rely on ladybird beetles which eat aphids. Spray only if many plants have 10-15 aphids per earhead: imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.25 ml per litre or thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.2 g per litre, in the evening.
prevention: Avoid very late sowing|Do not spray without need - natural enemies usually control aphids|Yellow sticky traps at the field edge help you monitor build up
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi crops (pau.edu); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: black and green small insects sucking on wheat ears, hands get sticky when touching the crop
label: wheat_aphid

symptoms_text: plants dry up in patches and come out easily when pulled, roots eaten away, white ants seen in the soil, worse in sandy unirrigated fields
label: wheat_termite
treatment: Irrigate immediately - termites move away from wet soil. Then apply chlorpyriphos 20 EC 1 litre per acre mixed with irrigation water through the water channel.
prevention: In termite prone fields treat seed with chlorpyriphos 20 EC 4 ml per kg before sowing|Use only well rotted FYM, never raw dung|Remove stubble and crop residue that attracts termites
source: PAU Package of Practices for Rabi crops (pau.edu); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: white ants eating wheat roots, drying plants scattered in the field that pull out easily
label: wheat_termite

symptoms_text: flowers do not open properly and look like a rosette, pink caterpillars inside green bolls, damaged seeds and stained lint
label: cotton_pink_bollworm
treatment: Set 8 pheromone traps per acre; when catches cross about 8 moths per trap for 3 nights, spray profenofos 50 EC 2 ml per litre or emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre. Pick and destroy rosette flowers and infested bolls every week.
prevention: End the crop by December-January and never keep it as ratoon|Destroy stalks and unopened bolls after the last picking|Use pheromone mating disruption ropes (PBKnot/SPLAT) where your department supplies them|Start trap monitoring from flowering stage
source: ICAR-CICR pink bollworm advisories (cicr.org.in); mating disruption field reports, Down To Earth / Krishak Jagat 2022-23

symptoms_text: bolls open badly with blackened spoiled lint late in the season, small pink worms found inside bolls
label: cotton_pink_bollworm

symptoms_text: tiny white flies rise in a cloud when the plant is shaken, leaves sticky with black sooty coating and turning yellow
label: cotton_whitefly
treatment: Spray neem oil 5 ml per litre with a little soap, or diafenthiuron 50 WP 1 g per litre, in the evening covering the underside of leaves. Avoid synthetic pyrethroids which flare up whitefly.
prevention: Put up yellow sticky traps 4-6 per acre|Remove alternate host weeds like kanghi (Abutilon) around the field|Avoid excess nitrogen|Sow recommended varieties at the recommended time
source: ICAR-CICR whitefly advisory for north zone cotton (cicr.org.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: cotton leaves yellow and sticky with small white insects underneath, black mould on leaf surface
label: cotton_whitefly

symptoms_text: leaves curl upward or downward with thick swollen veins, small cup like leafy growths on the underside, plant stunted
label: cotton_leaf_curl_virus
treatment: No spray can cure the virus. Pull out and bury badly affected plants early, and control the whitefly that spreads it (neem oil 5 ml per litre or diafenthiuron 50 WP 1 g per litre).
prevention: Grow leaf curl tolerant varieties recommended in north India|Control whitefly from the seedling stage|Remove weed hosts in and around the field|Avoid sowing next to an already infected field
source: ICAR-CICR cotton leaf curl disease advisories (cicr.org.in)

symptoms_text: cotton plant small with curled thick leaves and vein swelling, whiteflies present, few bolls
label: cotton_leaf_curl_virus

symptoms_text: leaf edges turn yellow then reddish brown and curl downwards like a cup, small green wedge shaped insects that walk sideways under leaves
label: cotton_jassid
treatment: Spray only when there are 2-3 jassids per leaf on many plants: flonicamid 50 WG 0.3 g per litre or imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.25 ml per litre.
prevention: Choose hairy leaf jassid tolerant varieties|Imidacloprid treated seed protects the first 40-50 days|Avoid excess nitrogen which makes leaves soft and attractive
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Cotton (agritech.tnau.ac.in); ICAR-CICR

symptoms_text: cotton leaves red at the edges and curling down, crop looks scorched, tiny green hoppers underneath
label: cotton_jassid

symptoms_text: angular water soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown to black, spots run along the veins, black lesions on stem and boll rot
label: cotton_bacterial_blight
treatment: Spray copper oxychloride 3 g per litre plus streptocycline 0.1 g per litre at the first sign and repeat after 10 days.
prevention: Use acid delinted certified seed|Rotate with non cotton crops for a season|Collect and burn infected plant debris after harvest
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Cotton (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: black angular spots on cotton leaves and black arm like patches on stems after rains
label: cotton_bacterial_blight

symptoms_text: dark brown spots with a ring pattern like a target on the older lower leaves, yellowing around the spots, leaves drop
label: tomato_early_blight
treatment: Remove the worst affected leaves. Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre; if it keeps spreading alternate with azoxystrobin 23 SC 1 ml per litre.
prevention: Do not grow tomato or potato in the same bed every season|Stake plants and keep lower leaves off the soil|Water at the base, not over the leaves|Use healthy seedlings
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Horticulture Crop Protection: Tomato (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: target like ring spots on tomato leaves starting from the bottom of the plant, spots also on stems and fruit base
label: tomato_early_blight

symptoms_text: large water soaked dark patches on leaves and stems during cool cloudy wet weather, white fungal ring under the leaf, fruits get greasy brown patches, spreads within days
label: tomato_late_blight
treatment: Act fast: remove infected parts and spray cymoxanil 8% + mancozeb 64% WP 3 g per litre; repeat after 10 days. The disease slows down in dry sunny weather.
prevention: Start protective mancozeb 2.5 g per litre sprays when the weather turns cool and cloudy|Avoid overhead evening irrigation|Space plants for air flow|Destroy volunteer potato and tomato plants nearby
source: ICAR-CPRI late blight management studies (cpri.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: tomato leaves turning black and rotting fast in foggy weather, brown firm patches spreading on green fruits
label: tomato_late_blight

symptoms_text: young leaves curl upward become small yellow and crinkled, plant stops growing and gives few fruits, whiteflies under leaves
label: tomato_leaf_curl_virus
treatment: No spray cures the virus. Remove and bury infected plants as soon as they are seen, and control whitefly with yellow sticky traps and neem oil 5 ml per litre.
prevention: Raise seedlings under a fine nylon net|Grow leaf curl tolerant hybrids|Hang yellow sticky traps from nursery stage itself|Keep the field and borders weed free
source: IIHR / TNAU Agritech Portal, tomato leaf curl management (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: tomato plants stunted with small curled yellow leaves and almost no fruit set, tiny white insects flying around
label: tomato_leaf_curl_virus

symptoms_text: round holes bored in fruits, caterpillar feeding with its head inside the fruit and body outside, damaged fruits rot and drop
label: tomato_fruit_borer
treatment: Hand pick and destroy damaged fruits and caterpillars. Spray HaNPV 250 LE 1 ml per litre or Bt 2 g per litre in the evening while larvae are small; if damage continues use chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC 0.3 ml per litre. Keep a 5-7 day gap between the last spray and picking.
prevention: Plant a row of marigold around tomato as a trap crop - the moths prefer laying eggs on it|Set pheromone traps 4-5 per acre|Put up bird perches|Do not repeat the same insecticide again and again
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; ICAR-NBAIR biocontrol recommendations (nbair.res.in)

symptoms_text: worms making holes in tomatoes and eating them from inside, half the fruit spoiled
label: tomato_fruit_borer

symptoms_text: plant wilts suddenly while still green without yellowing, cut stem dipped in a glass of clean water releases milky white threads
label: tomato_bacterial_wilt
treatment: No chemical cures it. Remove wilted plants along with root soil. Drench the remaining beds with bleaching powder solution and do not move soil from the affected patch to other beds.
prevention: Do not grow tomato, chilli, brinjal or potato in that field for 2-3 seasons|Use raised beds with good drainage|Use resistant varieties or grafted seedlings where available|Wash tools after working in an infected patch
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Horticulture Crop Protection: Tomato (agritech.tnau.ac.in); IIHR

symptoms_text: green tomato plants drooping and dying one by one though there is water in the field, roots look brown inside
label: tomato_bacterial_wilt

symptoms_text: nursery seedlings rot at the soil line, topple over and die in patches, worse in wet crowded beds
label: tomato_damping_off
treatment: Drench affected nursery beds with copper oxychloride 3 g per litre. Remove dead seedlings and reduce watering at once.
prevention: Raise the nursery on beds 10-15 cm high|Treat seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg or captan 2 g per kg|Do not sow too thick|Water in the morning only
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, nursery disease management (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: tomato seedlings falling over at ground level in the nursery with a rotten thin stem
label: tomato_damping_off

symptoms_text: dark water soaked patches at leaf tips and edges spreading very fast in cool cloudy drizzly weather, white fungal ring under the leaf, blackened stems and a rotten smell in the field
label: potato_late_blight
treatment: Spray cymoxanil 8% + mancozeb 64% WP 3 g per litre immediately and repeat after 10 days. If the tops are badly hit near maturity, cut and remove the haulm so the spores do not wash down and rot the tubers.
prevention: Begin protective sprays of mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre as soon as fog and cloudy weather set in|Plant healthy certified seed tubers|Make high ridges so rain cannot wash spores onto tubers|Follow the late blight alerts issued by your KVK or agriculture department
source: ICAR-CPRI late blight spray schedules (cpri.icar.gov.in)

symptoms_text: potato leaves turning black and rotting within a few days of foggy weather, tubers later show reddish brown dry rot under the skin
label: potato_late_blight

symptoms_text: angular dark brown spots with clear concentric rings on the older lower leaves, leaves yellow and dry from the bottom of the plant upwards
label: potato_early_blight
treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre at the first sign and repeat after 10-12 days if the spots increase.
prevention: Use healthy seed tubers|Keep the crop well fed and watered - weak plants get early blight first|Rotate with cereals|Destroy infected haulm after harvest
source: ICAR-CPRI; TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Potato (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: ring patterned brown spots on lower potato leaves in warm weather, plant drying from below
label: potato_early_blight

symptoms_text: hard black soil like crusts stuck on the tuber skin that do not wash off, sprouts from such tubers rot or carry brown sunken cankers
label: potato_black_scurf
treatment: Affected tubers are still safe to eat but must not be used as seed. For seed lots, dip tubers in 3% boric acid solution for 30 minutes and dry in shade before storing or planting.
prevention: Buy certified seed tubers|Rotate potato with cereals|Harvest soon after maturity - the longer tubers sit in soil the more scurf forms
source: ICAR-CPRI seed tuber health recommendations (cpri.icar.gov.in)

symptoms_text: black hard specks like stuck mud on potato tubers which do not rub off after washing
label: potato_black_scurf

symptoms_text: small green insects under potato leaves and sticky leaf surface, plants grown from own saved seed are weak with rolled or mottled leaves
label: potato_aphid_virus
treatment: Spray imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.25 ml per litre when aphids build up, especially in a crop kept for seed.
prevention: Replace your own saved seed with certified seed every 2-3 years|In seed crops cut the haulm when aphid counts rise as advised for your area|Pull out weak mosaic and leaf roll plants as soon as seen
source: ICAR-CPRI seed plot technique (cpri.icar.gov.in)

symptoms_text: potato plants from home saved seed growing weak with curled rolled leaves and low yield, small insects on the underside of leaves
label: potato_aphid_virus

symptoms_text: thin winding tunnels inside leaves, small caterpillars boring into tubers in the field and in the store, black droppings at the tunnel mouth
label: potato_tuber_moth
treatment: In the field, earth up immediately so no tuber stays exposed. In the store, keep tubers in thin layers and cover them with a 2 cm layer of dried neem or lantana leaves.
prevention: Never leave harvested tubers lying in the field overnight|Store only sound undamaged tubers in a cool dark airy place|Keep ridges high so tubers remain covered with soil
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Potato (agritech.tnau.ac.in); ICAR-CPRI

symptoms_text: small worms found in stored potatoes with tunnels and dirt inside, moths flying in the potato store
label: potato_tuber_moth

symptoms_text: leaves curl upward like a boat, become crinkled and brittle, tiny slender insects run inside leaf folds, flower buds drop and the plant looks bushy and stunted
label: chilli_thrips
treatment: Spray fipronil 5 SC 2 ml per litre or spinosad 45 SC 0.3 ml per litre covering the growing tips; repeat after 15 days if fresh curling continues.
prevention: Do not grow chilli after chilli in the same bed|Hang blue sticky traps for thrips|Light sprinkler irrigation raises humidity and checks thrips|Avoid excess nitrogen
source: ICAR-IIHR and TNAU chilli thrips recommendations (agritech.tnau.ac.in); Indian Journal of Entomology field trials

symptoms_text: chilli leaves curling up and crinkling, buds falling, plant stunted like churda murda
label: chilli_thrips

symptoms_text: leaves curl downward with long leaf stalks, turn dark green and shiny, growing point stops, no insect visible to the naked eye
label: chilli_mite
treatment: Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP 3 g per litre or spiromesifen 22.9 SC 1 ml per litre on the underside of leaves; repeat after 10 days.
prevention: Remember: downward curl means mites, upward curl means thrips - identify before spraying|Avoid dusty tracks beside the crop|Do not overuse synthetic pyrethroids which flare mites
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Horticulture Crop Protection: Chilli (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: chilli leaves bending down and turning dark shiny green, plant tip growth stopped, no pest seen
label: chilli_mite

symptoms_text: ripe fruits develop round sunken black spots with rings, fruits rot and fall, twig tips dry backwards from the top
label: chilli_anthracnose
treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruit. Spray azoxystrobin 23 SC 1 ml per litre or carbendazim 12% + mancozeb 63% WP 2.5 g per litre at flowering and again at fruit formation, 2-3 sprays 15 days apart.
prevention: Take seed only from healthy fruits or buy certified seed|Treat seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg or thiram 2 g per kg|Avoid overhead irrigation during fruiting|Prune and burn dried infected twigs
source: TNAU Agritech Portal; published Indian field trials on chilli anthracnose fungicides (azoxystrobin, carbendazim+mancozeb)

symptoms_text: black round sunken spots on red chilli fruits which spread and spoil the whole fruit, branch tips drying
label: chilli_anthracnose

symptoms_text: chilli nursery seedlings rot at the base and fall over in patches, more where beds stay wet
label: chilli_damping_off
treatment: Drench the nursery bed with copper oxychloride 3 g per litre and stop heavy watering. Remove dead seedlings.
prevention: Raise seedlings on raised beds or in trays|Treat seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg|Sow thin|Water only in the morning
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, nursery disease management (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: young chilli plants dying in the nursery with thin rotten stems near the soil
label: chilli_damping_off

symptoms_text: ragged holes and window like patches on whorl leaves, wet sawdust like droppings inside the funnel, caterpillar with an inverted Y mark on its head
label: maize_fall_armyworm
treatment: For small larvae drop dry sand or soil mixed with lime into the funnel. If more than 1 in 10 plants show fresh damage, spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre or spinetoram 11.7 SC 0.5 ml per litre directly into the whorl in the evening.
prevention: Set pheromone traps 4 per acre from the first week|Sow on time and together with neighbouring fields|Intercrop maize with pulses|Put up bird perches - birds pick larvae from whorls
source: ICAR fall armyworm advisory; Indian field efficacy trials (Florida Entomologist 2020; Maharashtra/TNAU trials)

symptoms_text: young maize funnel eaten with big ragged holes and moist frass like wet sawdust, worms hide deep in the whorl during the day
label: maize_fall_armyworm

symptoms_text: central shoot of young maize dries into a dead heart, rows of small shot holes appear across the leaf when it unfolds
label: maize_stem_borer
treatment: Spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC 0.3 ml per litre into the whorls 10-15 days after germination in borer prone areas. Remove and destroy dead hearts.
prevention: Sow early|Release Trichogramma egg parasitoid cards where available|Remove and destroy stubble after harvest|Intercrop with cowpea
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Maize (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: holes in straight lines across maize leaves and some plants with dried central shoots
label: maize_stem_borer

symptoms_text: long boat or cigar shaped grey brown dried patches on leaves starting from the lower leaves and moving up
label: maize_turcicum_blight
treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre at first appearance and repeat after 10-12 days if it spreads.
prevention: Grow tolerant hybrids|Rotate with non cereal crops|Bury or compost infected residue instead of leaving it on the field
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Maize (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: big long grey brown dry lesions on maize leaves, lower leaves drying first
label: maize_turcicum_blight

symptoms_text: third and fourth leaves dry first then the whole top, split cane shows red inside with white patches running crosswise, sour alcohol like smell
label: sugarcane_red_rot
treatment: No spray can cure red rot. Cut and burn affected clumps along with roots, and stop irrigation water flowing from the affected plot to healthy ones. Do not take a ratoon crop from an infected field.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties recommended by your sugar mill or university|Take setts only from healthy disease free fields|Dip setts in carbendazim 0.1% solution before planting|Rotate the field with rice or green manure for a season
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (sbi.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: cane drying from the top, inside of the stalk red with white cross bands and a smell like spoiled toddy
label: sugarcane_red_rot

symptoms_text: dead hearts in 1-3 month old cane that pull out easily and smell rotten, small holes with frass near the base of shoots
label: sugarcane_early_shoot_borer
treatment: Apply chlorantraniliprole 0.4 GR granules about 7.5 kg per acre near the cane rows and earth up. Remove and destroy dead hearts.
prevention: Cover the soil between rows with trash mulch - the moth avoids mulched fields|Plant early before hot weather|Earth up at the right stage|Release Trichogramma cards where available
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Sugarcane (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: young sugarcane shoots drying in the middle and coming out with a bad smell when pulled
label: sugarcane_early_shoot_borer

symptoms_text: a long black whip like structure comes out of the growing point of the cane instead of leaves, covered with black powder
label: sugarcane_smut
treatment: Cover the black whip with a bag before it sheds powder, pull out the whole clump and burn it. Do not keep a ratoon of a badly affected field.
prevention: Treat setts in hot water at 50 degrees C for 2 hours (or moist hot air at the mill) before planting|Use healthy seed cane from disease free nurseries|Grow resistant varieties
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (sbi.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: black whip like shoot growing from the top of sugarcane covered in dark dust
label: sugarcane_smut

symptoms_text: dead heart in grown cane that does not pull out easily, tunnels in the midrib of top leaves, side shoots sprout near the top giving a bunchy look
label: sugarcane_top_borer
treatment: Apply chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC 375 ml per hectare as soil drench near the rows at the recommended timing for your state, and cut out and destroy affected tops.
prevention: Remove egg masses seen on the underside of top leaves|Release Trichogramma or Isotima parasitoids where the department supplies them|Avoid excess nitrogen late in the season
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Sugarcane (agritech.tnau.ac.in)

symptoms_text: top of the cane dried with bunchy side shoots and tunnels seen in the leaf midribs
label: sugarcane_top_borer

symptoms_text: dense colonies of grey green insects covering flowering shoots and pods, plants sticky with honeydew, shoots curl and dry
label: mustard_aphid
treatment: Spray only when there are 50-60 aphids per 10 cm of the top shoot on many plants: thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.2 g per litre or imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.25 ml per litre, late in the evening to protect honeybees.
prevention: Sow by mid October - an early sown crop largely escapes aphids|Do not spray without crossing the threshold, ladybird beetles eat huge numbers of aphids|Yellow sticky traps help you watch the build up
source: ICAR-DRMR, Bharatpur (drmr.res.in); ICAR Journal of Oilseed Brassica aphid ETL 50-60 per 10 cm shoot

symptoms_text: sarson flowering tops fully covered with small grey insects, plants sticky and shoots bending
label: mustard_aphid

symptoms_text: round dark brown to black spots with concentric rings on leaves and later on pods, spots join and leaves dry
label: mustard_alternaria_blight
treatment: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g per litre at first appearance and repeat after 15 days if the spots increase.
prevention: Sow on time|Use clean certified seed|Avoid evening irrigation in cloudy spells|Remove crop debris after harvest
source: ICAR-DRMR, Bharatpur (drmr.res.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: target like dark ring spots on mustard leaves and pods in humid weather
label: mustard_alternaria_blight

symptoms_text: creamy white raised pustules on the underside of leaves, flower heads become swollen twisted green structures called stag heads
label: mustard_white_rust
treatment: Spray metalaxyl + mancozeb 72 WP 2.5 g per litre when white pustules appear, and nip off and destroy the swollen deformed flower heads.
prevention: Treat seed with metalaxyl 35 SD 6 g per kg|Sow on time|Rotate fields|Avoid irrigating during flowering in disease prone humid weeks
source: ICAR-DRMR; Indian field trials showing metalaxyl+mancozeb 0.2% effective against white rust

symptoms_text: white paint like blisters under mustard leaves and deformed swollen flower shoots with no pods
label: mustard_white_rust

symptoms_text: red and black patterned bugs sucking sap on young seedlings and again on ripening pods, patches of seedlings dry up
label: mustard_painted_bug
treatment: Collect and destroy bugs in the morning. If seedlings are dying, spray malathion 50 EC 2 ml per litre; repeat on harvested windrows if bugs attack there.
prevention: Sow early|Give the first light irrigation 3-4 weeks after sowing which destroys many eggs|Thresh the harvested crop quickly, do not leave heaps in the field for days
source: ICAR-DRMR, Bharatpur (drmr.res.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: black and red small bugs in groups on mustard seedlings, seedlings drying in patches
label: mustard_painted_bug

symptoms_text: green or brown striped caterpillars first eat leaves then bore round holes in pods and eat the grain with the head inside the pod
label: gram_pod_borer
treatment: While larvae are small spray HaNPV 250 LE 1 ml per litre or neem seed kernel extract 5%. If 1-2 larvae per metre row remain at flowering and podding, spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre.
prevention: Set pheromone traps 4-5 per acre|Fix T shaped bird perches 8-10 per acre - birds pick the caterpillars|Intercrop gram with coriander or linseed|Do not repeat the same insecticide season after season
source: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur IPM package for chickpea (iipr.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: worms making round holes in chana pods and eating the seed from inside, green caterpillars also eating leaves
label: gram_pod_borer

symptoms_text: plants droop and dry in patches, colour dull green turning straw, split root shows dark brown to black streaks inside, seedlings and podding stage worst hit
label: gram_fusarium_wilt
treatment: A wilted plant cannot be saved. Pull out and remove affected plants. For the next crop treat seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg plus carboxin + thiram 2 g per kg and grow a wilt resistant variety such as JG 315.
prevention: Sow from the last week of October onwards when the soil has cooled|In wilt sick fields rotate with cereals for 2-3 years|Use resistant varieties|Avoid moisture stress followed by irrigation shocks
source: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur (iipr.icar.gov.in); published Indian trials of Trichoderma + carboxin seed treatment for chickpea wilt

symptoms_text: chana plants wilting and drying in patches in the field, inside of the root black when split open
label: gram_fusarium_wilt

symptoms_text: young seedlings topple and die, white fungal threads and small mustard seed like balls seen at the collar near the soil, worse in moist soil with undecomposed stubble
label: gram_collar_rot
treatment: Remove dead seedlings together with the fungus and surrounding soil, and stop heavy irrigation. Gap fill with seed treated with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg.
prevention: Treat all seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg before sowing|Remove or burn undecomposed stubble before sowing|Do not sow too deep|Avoid heavy irrigation at seedling stage
source: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur (iipr.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: chana seedlings dying at one month with white fungus and tiny round balls at the stem base near soil
label: gram_collar_rot

symptoms_text: plants dry up suddenly in patches at flowering and podding during a warm dry spell, roots look grey brittle and shredded with no rot smell
label: gram_dry_root_rot
treatment: Plants that have dried cannot recover. A light irrigation at pod filling during a dry spell reduces further plant deaths.
prevention: Sow on time so pod filling escapes peak heat|Treat seed with Trichoderma viride 4 g per kg|Choose tolerant varieties|Avoid moisture stress at flowering and podding
source: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur (iipr.icar.gov.in)

symptoms_text: chana drying suddenly near maturity in hot dry weather, roots brittle and grey that break easily
label: gram_dry_root_rot
